headline: Chicago November ferrous scrap settles higher: shred up $30, busheling up $20
detail: Mills paid $20-30/gt more for November scrap. In Chicago, shredded rose $30/gt and busheling $20/gt, and P&S and rail grades stayed short. Firm mill demand and slow inbound flows are holding Midwest scrap up going into winter.

headline: LME copper falls about 1.3% to $13,712 after hot US inflation report
detail: October CPI came in above forecast, and Fed officials sounded hawkish, so traders added bets on a December rate hike and LME copper settled down 1.27%. Chinese buyers are also balking at high prices and premiums, which points to softer copper scrap bids in the near term.

headline: Nucor lifts HRC spot price $15 to $1,295/st, the 17th straight weekly increase
detail: Nucor raised its weekly hot-rolled coil price again, with lead times holding at 3-5 weeks. US HRC is trading about $1,340-1,400/st. Strong sheet prices keep EAF mills hungry for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Hot October CPI makes a December Fed hike look nearly certain
detail: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against 0.3% expected, and core prices rose 0.3% against 0.2%. Futures now put a December hike at about 89%, with some bets on a half-point move. The dollar index firmed to about 102 and 2-year yields jumped. Higher rates and a firmer dollar usually weigh on copper, aluminum and scrap prices.

headline: LME aluminum drops to three-week low below $3,000 on Chinese exports and Iran de-escalation
detail: Three-month aluminum fell 2.3% to about $2,995/t, now about 21% below June's four-year high. Chinese exports are up 18% this year and Middle East supply is returning faster than expected, so aluminum scrap values face pressure, although LME stocks remain low.

headline: US and China extend their trade truce two more months, to January 10
detail: China paused some critical-mineral export controls and its 24% tariff on US goods for two more months, though a 10% duty remains. The US extended 178 Section 301 tariff exclusions on Chinese goods. This avoids a near-term escalation that could have rattled metals markets and supply chains.

headline: Midterm results raise hopes of Canada tariff relief that could shrink the Midwest premium
detail: The Midwest aluminum premium had eased to $1.12/lb from a record $1.19 in May. After Democratic wins, traders expect pressure for a US-Canada deal on the 50% tariff. Any decline is expected to be gradual, but scrap brokers cut prices quickly the last time a deal was floated.

headline: Platinum and palladium fall back from recent highs after the CPI report
detail: Platinum fell about 2.4% from a three-week high near $1,587/oz, and palladium was 3% below last week's $1,066 high, as rate-hike bets rose. Lower PGM prices mean lower catalytic converter payouts.

headline: Fed's Waller says a half-point December hike should be on the table
detail: Fed Governor Waller said a 25bp hike could put the Fed's credibility at risk if core inflation stays hot. A larger hike would support the dollar and tighten credit for metal buyers and end users.

headline: China's October trade jumps; exports up about 29%, imports up about 35%
detail: Customs data showed October exports up 28.7% and imports up 34.7% from a year earlier in yuan terms, with auto exports up 37.6%. China's trade surplus for the year has passed $1 trillion. Strong imports signal solid raw-material demand, while the auto export surge adds pressure on global car makers.

headline: China's iron ore imports slip in October while steel exports stay near 10 million tonnes
detail: Iron ore imports fell to about 105.7 million tonnes, down 3.8% from September and 5.1% from a year ago. Steel exports were about 9.85 million tonnes, slightly above last year. Softer ore buying points to cautious mills, and steady exports keep cheap Chinese steel weighing on world prices.

headline: New Democratic Congress may target tariffs, but Trump's veto limits what it can do
detail: Democrats take over both chambers in January and plan to go after tariffs, more likely one tariff at a time than with a broad overhaul. Without two-thirds majorities to override a veto, the Section 232 steel, aluminum and copper tariffs that support domestic prices likely stay in place for now.

headline: Codelco cuts 2026 copper guidance to about 1.2 Mt and admits overstating past output
detail: Chile's state miner lowered its 2026 target from 1.34 Mt. It confirmed that 42,100 t of 2024-25 output was overstated and dropped its goal of 1.7 Mt a year by 2030. Lower supply from the world's top copper producer supports copper prices over the longer term.

headline: Gold and silver fall as October CPI beats forecasts
detail: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against 0.3% expected, raising bets on a December Fed hike. Gold fell about 1.8%, silver about 2.3% and copper about 1%. A hawkish Fed and a stronger dollar weigh on the whole metals complex.

headline: Cleveland-Cliffs and USW reach four-year labor deals covering about 12,000 workers
detail: The tentative deals cover Cliffs steel and mining sites in Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Minnesota and Michigan, pending ratification. They remove a strike risk at major Midwest steelmaking and iron ore operations.

headline: Mortgage rates post biggest one-day jump in over a month after CPI
detail: The average 30-year fixed rate rose to about 7.30%, up 0.12 point in a day after the hot inflation report. Higher borrowing costs further cool homebuilding and the demand for wire, pipe and rebar that comes with it.

headline: Stellantis sells idled Brampton, Ontario car plant to a defense contractor
detail: Stellantis sold the Brampton assembly plant to armored-vehicle maker Roshel, and more than 2,200 laid-off auto workers face an uncertain future. It is another lost North American assembly plant, which means less auto stamping and production scrap in the region.

headline: Sibanye-Stillwater cuts US PGM output forecast after Montana strike
detail: Sibanye lowered 2026 output from its Montana mines to 245,000-255,000 oz, from 280,000-300,000 oz, after a five-week strike, and raised its cost guidance. Less US-mined palladium and platinum lends some support to PGM prices.

headline: Stellantis keeps Windsor minivan and Charger plant down for a fourth straight week
detail: Production at Windsor Assembly, which has about 6,400 workers, is idled through the week of Nov 9, and Stellantis cites demand and tariffs. Long shutdowns cut flat-rolled steel and aluminum demand and the flow of prompt industrial scrap from feeder plants.

headline: Copper slips near $13,900 on election jitters as US refined-copper tariff talk resurfaces
detail: LME copper fell about 1% to $13,897 around the midterm results. A report said a US tariff on refined copper imports is under discussion, which could widen the Comex-LME gap and change US copper scrap spreads.

headline: China factory prices rise at their fastest pace in over four years
detail: Producer prices rose 5.7% from a year earlier in October, driven mainly by oil and energy costs, while consumer inflation eased to 0.7%. Squeezed factory margins and weak households argue against a big construction-led stimulus that would lift steel demand.

headline: Canada extends and widens its tariff-relief program to mid-2028
detail: Ottawa extended its remission program, which has helped firms move away from US steel suppliers, to June 2028. It also widened the program to more manufacturing, farm and mining inputs. That supports the cross-border steel trade shifting away from US mills.

headline: Residential construction sheds most jobs since 2021 while nonresidential adds
detail: Residential construction cut 16,400 jobs in October, its biggest drop since March 2021, while nonresidential added about 13,300. Housing is weakening, and commercial and industrial work such as data centers is carrying construction-steel demand.

headline: Court fight continues over $18B Grayslake data center as building proceeds
detail: A Lake County judge heard the village's bid to dismiss a neighbor lawsuit against the T5 data center project and will rule by Dec 30. Construction is already underway. Large local data center builds are a major source of steel and copper demand in the Chicago area.

headline: Nickel jumps to five-week high as Indonesia cracks down on a major ore trader
detail: LME nickel rose 3.8% to $16,375/t after Indonesia's forestry task force moved against firms tied to a large nickel ore trader. Tighter Indonesian supply can support nickel and stainless scrap values.

headline: Iron ore slips as northern China orders pollution-related steel curbs
detail: Tangshan and Handan started emergency air-pollution measures that usually force steel output cuts. Dalian ore fell to about 684.5 yuan and China's hot-metal output hit its lowest since March, a sign of weak demand for steelmaking raw materials worldwide.
